sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Good.
Good afternoon, Andy.
Hi, Neil.
How you doing?
I'm not too bad, how are you?
Yeah, sorry I'm a little bit late.
I've got somebody locked up their email accounts just trying to fix it.
Yeah, I'm not too bad actually.
Excuse.
Excuse my business.
Just been at the gym.
No, all good, all good, yeah.
Yeah.
Well, thank you.
Thanks for taking the time.
I'm sure you have lots of chats like this, but.
Yeah, thanks for responding to my message.
Yeah, no worries.
Interested to sort of chat really and kind of figure out what it is that you're.
You're looking for.
So.
So yeah, be good to hear a bit about you.
Happy to give you a bit more about ourselves.
I don't know how much you know about Capital A.
Yeah, yeah, I mean, I know.
I don't know, maybe we start there.
I mean, I've.
I've kind of followed a little bit of your work in the M and A space, I guess, just.
Yeah, I spent my whole career in marketing services really.
So I kind of see, see people, people exit and lots of success stories and the players within that space.
And I think from my perspective, you know, I've, I've launched an agency about 16 months ago now, which is, which is going great.
Obviously, you know, we're, we're building a roadmap with an exit in mind, you know, so we're, we're early days, but obviously we're conscious.
We need to be thinking 24 months ahead anyway.
So that's kind of part of my thinking anyway.

But, but really I was, I was keen to apply some of my experience, agency side, both, both at Holdcos and Indies and really just learn a little bit more about the M and A space, if I'm being perfectly frank.
So it wasn't, I guess I wasn't messaging you to be like, hey, look, we're ready to, we're ready to do a deal.
I speak to founders on a regular basis.
I've been at Adweek this week.
I was there yesterday, I was there this morning.
You know, I know lots of people who are looking both from an acquisition side but also just, you know, to kind of.
Yeah, to kind of realize their dreams as well.
So I speak to lots of brands and lots of agencies and I'm quite well connected.

And actually what I thought was I know some people similar to myself who've been sort of 15 plus years in the industry, you know, do operate in, you know, working alongside players like yourselves in some kind of capacity.
And for me, just Being purely selfish, I was like, actually how can I learn?
Get a better understanding of what you do and is there a role I can play?
So I've met a couple of agencies this week and I've got a pretty good grasp of the landscape and what the challenges are strategically, operationally.
And I'd just be interested to hear how you guys approach that space.
And actually is there value in what I know and who I know and how can I plug into the world that you operate?
So yeah, that sort of my cards on the table, Andy.
All right, so, so just let me just try and get my head around where you're at.
So ruffle is your full time passion, should we call it?
You're 18 months in, but you're, you're historically involved with marketing services, so you just worked for other people previously.
And this is your first agency, is that right?
Yeah, this is the first agency that I own previously.
I've ran agencies, um, so I've been managing directors of production companies.
I've led them to, you know, numerous awards.
I've worked at Havas, so I've worked at some of the Holcos.
Then I kind of went down the indie route.
I've been managing director for a few sort of fast growth independent agencies.
Had a shareholding in one and.
Yeah, and led those to kind of numerous agency of the year awards, to be honest with you.
And then I realized I should just do this myself.
So yeah, like I say, we, we've literally just filed our first year's accounts.
So we are small.
We've got a headcount of three.
We've got a turnover of about 660k for first year.
Our EBITDA is 59 off that, so whatever that is, 338 or something.
So like pretty profitable.
First year good.
First year solid, you know, modest.
But we're, there's, there's three.
Right.
So it's, it is what it is and we're moving from a passion and a lifestyle to scaling it and we know what our roadmap is and we think, and I think we know how to get there.
So I'm a commercial operator, so I know how to grow a business.
So I think hopefully we'll be looking to sort of double that this year is the plan.
All right, so, and then your interest in working with Capital A is on what, in what capacity is that?
As somebody that can refer leads within your network or are you looking to be involved more heavily than that?
I'll be honest, I'm, I'm, I'm I'm flexible.
And it was really just to kickstart a conversation, I think.
I know, I know people, I know agencies that are, that are looking, you know, now's the time, right?
Is, is.
I guess there's no better time than now.

So I think it's like I speak to a lot of founders and other agencies often, you know, we do work with other agencies and it's sort of getting, it's whether I can help in any kind of advisory capacity or maybe it is sending these to you guys.

I think I'd want to get a better understanding of your world because I'll be honest, you know, I'm not, I'm not an accountant by trade, but if there's some kind of value that I can add in terms of, look, just being selfish, I want to future proof myself and I want to understand a little bit more and I'm trying to constantly grow.

So for me it's actually, you know, I spoke to a founder of an independent network group who I know is probably looking for an exit speak to lots of people I know who are good up and coming agencies because I'm pitching against them or I know them.
So it's actually how could I potentially whether that's just in a, some kind of part time capacity referral, some kind of way.
I'd love to, I'd love to have my one foot in the world that you guys operate in just to broaden my horizons because you know, I probably won't be an agency world forever.
So I've always got a mind on that as well.
Okay, cool.
Yeah, so.
Well, just to let you know, my background is possibly similar to yours, so I'm not the accountant type either.
But we do have people on our team that are more sort of aligned with those kinds of roles.
But we do also have senior advisors, what we call senior advisors, which people are more experienced in the industry, but they do tend to work on deals and projects with us.
So I'll give you an example.

So we have a client that's buying certain types of immersive experience businesses in the US we have somebody on our team who's worked on a few different deals with us buy side deals, but this is her expertise.
So our team provide all the leads to her and she picks out the ones that look like good targets for acquisitions.
She speaks to them directly and if they look like a good fit and it's a good time for everybody, then we get a call with our client and we progress it, you know, through, through that process.
If they like them.
You know, we move through the process to try and make that an acquisition.
On the sell side, we have clients that are looking to sell and it's kind of the same process but opposite where our team are generating leads with buyers.
Buyers obviously express an interest and then if we have an advisor that's particularly good in that area, then sometimes they're working on the sell side as well.
So is that the kind of capacity or is it more about the referral side of things?
Because again, we have people that are in our network who can refer, you know, agency owners, like you're saying.
And we just pay them a percentage on, on those introductions.

So we take a percentage on, on our retainers which are guaranteed because obviously they become a client, we charge them the fees or they, they take a percentage on the deal which is further down the road, sometimes a year away.
I'm not guaranteed.
So it's either or of those really.
And there's, I mean there's, there's plenty of it to be done.
If I'm being honest myself as well.
You know, having we generate the biz dev within our team, we've got some tools that we, we own that we've acquired for deal flows.
So for instance, we've got a company called dealengines.com which has the, the tech to generate those leads as well.
So we, we do generate a lot of leads, but it's more about how many calls I can do.
And you know, I'm obviously working on deals as well that are closing or get to the close stage.
And then that's where my focus is, is getting those over the line because they can be, you know, 200, 300, 500 grand win fees.
So we're more focused on those than just generating new business all the time.
So yeah, where does your, your interest really sit?
I mean it might well be the latter.
Just.
And you can, you can maybe correct me if I'm wrong.
So probably had two conversations in the last couple of weeks with sort of founders and CEOs of sort of 100 person agencies.
Some have sort of sub brands within that, within sort of specialist disciplines.
And some of those disciplines are kind of hot, hot topic right now.
So there's one where I know that a, that a deal fell through, but they are looking to, to sell.
There's another one where I know they've built a bit of proprietary kit in preparation.
So they're sort of, they're sort of doing the, the playbook right.
I guess to, to kind of increase their multiple.
So Certainly in the last couple of weeks I've had two conversations where I know that they're, you know, that's what I would describe as a, a cold lead.
Right.
And it's whether, whether I can bring those to the table, whether I can facilitate them a bit more and hand them over.
And as you say, maybe it's, maybe it's a relationship that's, that's built on the latter option.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.
All right, well, happy to set something up like that if that's what, what you think is going to work for you.
Don't want to distract you from building raffle.
Yeah, yeah, no, I mean, I, Yeah, I mean that's, that's a fair point as well.
I think we're, you know, Ruffles.
Ruffles going great.
And I think we're, we're, we're in a good place.
And I think for me it's, I'm always thinking, what's next?
You know, so for Ruffle, it's, you know, geographies and service lines and things of that nature.

But at the same time, as an individual, I'm also thinking about what's, what's next for me, you know, so it's, it's about sort of future proofing myself, I guess, to, to a certain point and sort of, you know.
Yeah, I'm losing my hair, so I probably won't be an agency, well forever.
So it's like, what's going to be the next thing?
Right.
And for me, if I can build, you know, even just having a conversation with you today is great.
If we can, if I can build a rapport and kind of just build, build a bit more of a deeper understanding within M A.
I think that would be, that would be great for me.
Certainly that's the area where I want to take Ruffle anyway.
And perhaps an exercise of this nature will, will benefit Ruffle at the same time.
So it's kind of two pronged really.
Okay.
What's your involvement with.
With ruffle?
Sorry?
I said raffle.
It's my handwriting.
I was looking at.
What's your involvement with Ruffle on a day to day basis then?
Are you, are you actually in the trenches or is it more that you have a team and you're taking the margin?
No, I'm in the trenches, so to speak.
So yeah, I'm sort of the face, I guess so.
I'm sort of.
There's three co founders.
I'm pretty much more of the sales and marketing and financial board really.
So bringing in leads and a Bit of client service.
So I'm sort of, you know, I was at Adweek this week and so I sort of do a lot of hitting, hitting the road I guess, and speaking to brands and agencies directly and sort of winning business that way.
And then it kind of goes into our workflow and it's.
I'm not on the delivery side and then I'll come in at the end and take, take the client to lunch.
Yeah.
So.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.
All right, interesting.
Well, let me have a think how it could work beyond just the referrals because if you're looking to learn more of the ropes then really that doesn't happen just in a referral.
That happens in the more day to day conversations, you know, particularly the negotiation part of it once somebody has made an offer or that part.
Yeah, I mean, I think again, you know, I'm not.
I don't know how you, you sort of run things.

I mean I, I'd love to learn and you know, I'm not, you know, I, I guess I have a certain amount of time on my hands so I have other sort of ventures and you know, I'm a trustee of a charity and do mentorship and things sort of various, various fingers in various pies.
I, I suppose all within the broader sector anyway.
So it's all, it all feeds into one.
So for me, if, if there was an opportunity where I can lend some of my time and, and vice versa, even if that's just on a time basis whereby I can learn some of those ropes, I mean that would be.
That would be amazing for me.
You know, I'm also exploring doing a.
An MBA as well later on in the year just to again future proof.
So for me it's.
There is a self sort of development piece to this but it's all feeding into the same beast anyway.
So I guess for me it's.
Yeah, I didn't know how responsive you would be.
Um, so kind of setting up a call.
So.
And I actually didn't realize you guys owned agency.
Is it Agencies co the.
Yeah, I didn't realize that was you guys.
And that's a, that's a pretty, pretty kind of nifty, nifty site you set up.
So.
Yeah, if it is.

If there is an opportunity where I can really like kind of deepen my understanding and kind of get involved, whether it's just on an advisory or mentoring or shadowing or whatever that might look like, I'd be totally open to that.
Like honestly.
Andy.
Well, I guess that there is a lot to to learn.
But in all sort of, you know, the reality is with this work is beyond the spreadsheet stuff.
It is purely about relationships and almost mediation.

And you talk about mentorship, a lot of it is a bit like being at somebody's therapist, you know, because you're basically guiding somebody through a mental breakdown while they split up with the, you know, the, the love of their life and give it to somebody else and watch somebody else go off to.
Into the sunset with, with their dream.
So there, there is a, a lot of sort of support through that and that's a big part of it.
And so for me, you know, somebody like yourself who's been maybe not through a process, but certainly has grown businesses, that, that's a big part of it.

And that's why particularly Heather, who's on our team, she's based in New York, has been sort of really pivotal in some of the work that we've done with the agencies that we've been buying for, for clients, because you're basically, you know, helping people split up with the, with the, you know, their baby.
So.
And because Heather in particular is so experienced, I mean, she was part of the mill.
I don't if you know, the mill, but we were bought by Technicolor, so she was the MD there.
And so just being able to sort of lean into that experience herself has been sort of really good for our clients or the targets of our clients.
So there is definitely some of that you can bring to the table.
Also, I'm trying to do more, more work in the UK.
We're probably about 95 in the US so having somebody with your experience here.
We do work with a guy called Andy Hart as well, who's like a, he's a ex vice president of marketing at Microsoft, so he's got a huge network as well.
And he refers quite a bit of work in actually.
So, yeah, look flexible as well.
Definitely interested on something.
I, I guess I get that you want to learn the ropes or you want to, you know, you want to sort of have a bit personal development, but certainly doing deals is where you kind of get it.
You know, I think that's what I'm ultimately trying to say is like the referral part of it is great, but you're not going to learn anything.
It's being sat on the calls with the people that are interested in selling.

So it, it could be that we do something along the lines of, yes, there's a referral fee to get dibs on some of the retainer, but beyond that, if you wanted to sit through a process, and obviously I can either mentor you through that or the first few ones, probably you're just sitting on the calls and shadowing.
But it's not complicated.
It is just mediation really and, and guiding people through the introductions and, you know, seeing how they go and, and being a listening ear after those calls have happened.
And then my team are obviously just doing the work and generating the leads and the interest and all of that side of things.
So, yeah, just about nudging a deal to the close.
Yeah, yeah.
I mean it sounds, it sounds of, of massive interest to me.

I mean that softer side, right, is obviously where, where I'd come to the fore, you know, rather than sort of the pure numbers piece and think I've been involved in some conversations on the, on that investment piece.
So I was part of an agency called Kula that, that got sort of minority investment from.
Oh God, who was it?
Growth Capital Partners.
So again, it's kind of.
I've been involved in some of those conversations at an early stage, but ultimately that wasn't my business, so I was quickly sidelined.
So.
So yeah, and again, I've, I've been, I've been on the end of the phone when it' wrong and people have been interested.
So.
But again, it's, it's, it's typically not been me soaking up that information.
So I think, I mean that would, that sounds like if that is a route that would be really good.
And I think it is interesting what you say around.
Yeah.
People letting go of their baby.
Right.
And sort of, sort of hand holding through that process, which again is not dissimilar skill set to me.
Handholding a client through, you know, you know, an advertising campaign, right, that takes six months to delivery.
It's still, it's still, you know, there's tears, there's highs, there's lows and etc.
Etc.

So I feel like my skill set and my understanding and my network, there is a, there is a bit of a mirror there and I think it's just, it's understanding those nuts and bolts and that granular detail which I just don't have.
So, yeah, I mean, I'd love to continue, continue talking, whatever, however that takes place.
Yeah, cool.
All right, let.
Like I said, let, Let me just kind of have a think about.
We're in a bit of a.
So changing of the, the guard on my team as well.
I've just parted ways of.
With somebody on the west coast.
He's been with us for a while.
Who's quite senior and we've got a ton of new, new clients that were onboarding this week and next week.
So it could be that now is the right time basically for having somebody that can babysit some clients through a process.
And like I say, it's not terribly complicated.
It is really just being a sounding board a lot of it and the rest of it is just like a, it's like a numbered process with doing this, then this, then this, then this.
It's not, it's not that we, you know, we, we are, you know, officially we're a business broker and there's not a huge amount that we do.
The, the actual buying process is driven by the buyers.
We have to find the buyers and then kind of hand hold our client through that nervous breakdown.
But actually the buyers are doing the numbers.
We're not running any numbers, not particularly anyway, but there's a bit of preparation before we take a seller to the market.
And again that is done by our investment bankers and they are for the most part based in India.
We've got a couple of guys in the UK and the US but we've got an, you know, we've got this great guy that works for Shams.
He's based in Mumbai.
He's an mba, he's an investment banker.
He's worked at some huge banks.
But, but he runs the numbers.
You know, we don't have to do any of that sort of stuff and to be honest with you, it's pretty boring and it's not very interesting.
You know, the, the, the people that want those numbers tend to be on the capital side.
You know, people that are going to do the debt provision, then they want to see that.
So, but most of the people we deal with, they don't care about that stuff.
They're just gun ho agency owners that just want to buy this and that and this and that and we're there to just provide those routes to, to getting their vision done.
So.
Yeah, okay.
Okay.
Well, I mean it sounds, yeah, I mean, look, I appreciate time.
It sounds, it sounds pretty positive.
I think, I think certainly my expertise is UK market.
I mean interestingly, Ruffle do we probably do 10% of our work in, in the US but, but 90% UK and the majority of my experience is, is UK agencies and that landscape.
So yeah, I think, I think I could, I think there's some value certainly in the, in the people that I know and the conversations I'm having.
It's a little bit like I have these conversations and I don't know what to do with that information.
Right.
I'm like, you know what I mean?
It's like people are sort of what their plans are.
And I'm like, that's great.
And then what do I do with that?
You know?
Well, next steps with your 100 person agency.
So let's take as an example.
You know, they've been through a process and this happens to all the time.
Agency founders go through a process, nothing happens at the end of it, and then they come to us or they go to another M and A advisor.
You know, there is no 100% close rate.
It's like about 20, 30%.
So.
Okay.
So, yeah, I mean, bringing them to another M and A advisory is pretty straightforward.
We rely on referrals.
We get them from lawyers and accountants that are in the industry or other people that have been through our process and sold and they get referred in.
So, yeah, I mean, the next steps for us would be to have a conversation with them.
You would get a percentage on the referral, which usually is a couple of grand on those initial fees if they sign up as a full client.
So, yeah, we could just, we could get started with stuff like that for sure.
Okay, cool.
Okay.
Is there anything, is there anything that would be useful for me to, to share with you or should I just give you a bit of time to, to mullet over?
Well, I guess it's interest level because obviously you're building ruffle.
What I don't like doing is getting in the way of founders, you know, goals.
But if it's kind of, you know, the age, the agency slog is really difficult.
Not that M and A is particularly easy, but it's a.
It's a bit more scalable maybe in some ways, but yeah, I guess.
Look, we've had this call now, you know that I'm definitely interested or open to, to figuring something out.
So, yeah, let me, let me know what your thoughts are and we can go, we can go from there, but certainly I'll.
Yeah, I'll be in touch.
And let's try and get an agreement in place for these leads that you've got from this week.
Okay?
Okay, splendid.
All right, well, let's do that and yeah, sort of just follow up on email and we can, we can just kind of move things forward.
Yeah, definitely.
Brilliant.
Right.
Nice one, Neil.
Thanks for reaching out.
Yeah, likewise.
Appreciate your time.
We'll speak soon.
Cheers.

summary.action_items:
**Andy Day**
Think about how a collaboration with Neil could work beyond just referrals (15:46)
Follow up with Neil regarding an agreement for the leads he currently has (27:12)
Consider how Neil might help 'babysit' clients through the M&A process during team changes (22:19)

**Neil van Ginsburg**
Follow up with Andy via email to move the potential collaboration forward (27:12)
Share details of the agency leads he mentioned from Adweek (26:10)
summary.overview: The Exploratory Business Development Meeting between Neil Ginsburg and Andy Day focused on potential collaboration opportunities in the M&A space. Neil Ginsburg, founder of the agency Ruffle, shared his background in marketing and expressed interest in leveraging his connections with agency founders seeking acquisitions or exits. Ruffle has achieved impressive early results, generating £660K in turnover with a 33% margin, and Neil aims to double its growth this year. Andy Day outlined Capital A's M&A operations and suggested a partnership where Neil could shadow calls and earn referral fees while expanding his knowledge of the M&A process. Both agreed on the importance of relationship management in M&A transactions and discussed Neil potentially playing a supportive role during team transitions at Capital A. They concluded with actionable next steps, including Neil following up with leads and exploring how their collaboration could evolve.
summary.short_summary: Neil Ginsburg, founder of Ruffle, met with Andy Day to explore collaboration opportunities in the M&A space. Neil shared his extensive marketing experience and the impressive early results of Ruffle, which generated £660K in turnover with a 33% margin in its first year. He expressed a desire to learn about M&A processes while leveraging his connections with agency founders seeking acquisitions or exits. Andy outlined Capital A's operations, emphasizing the importance of relationship management in M&A, and suggested that Neil could shadow calls to gain insights and earn referral fees. Both parties acknowledged the potential for Neil to support Capital A during its team transitions and agreed on actionable next steps, including Neil following up with leads and discussing further collaboration.
